_comment: MASTER SYLLABUS TEMPLATE — Populated verbatim from /mnt/project/uace_LatinLanguage.pdf

attitudes: Appreciation of Roman culture and heritage

themes.theme_description: Foundation grammar covering Latin accidence, parts of speech, and initial syntax skills required for constructing and analysing Latin sentences.

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates a strong grasp by accurately applying Latin vocabulary, morphology, and syntax in order to construct/ produce and analyse Latin sentences across various textual contexts.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a. create nouns from verbs in Latin scripts
b. Use nouns to describe the state of other nouns related to social life
a. explain how the adjectives agree in gender, number and case of the nouns they describe
b. decline adjectives in the three degrees (positive, comparative and superlative)
c. use adjectives to describe Roman cultural events using apposition technique
a. form adverbs and categorize them (as adverbs of manner, time, place, frequency, degree, and probability) demonstrating an understanding of their functions
a. use adverbs to explain and modify actions in the Roman and contemporary living culture

suggested_learning_activities.description: Read a chosen Latin text and identify verbal nouns and common suffixes used to form nouns (e.g., -ndum, -or, -tio, -tor, -trix, -sor, -tura, -ium)
In groups, discuss how verb roots change when forming nouns, with examples (e.g., amor from amare)
Write sentences using verbal nouns
In pairs, interpret in Latin each other's English sentences using verbal nouns

From a chosen text, identify nouns that describe the state of other nouns, i.e. by apposition (Caesar rex) or genitive case (Dux militum), predicate (Caesar est rex.), ablative of description, dative of purpose
Generate sentences using nouns to describe the state of other nouns in social life
In the provided text, where adjectives of the third declension are not declined, align the gender, number and case of each to match the nouns they describe
In groups use adjectives to describe various objects in classroom/at home/of the body arts/environment/places
From a provided text, identify the adjectives in their different degrees (longus, longior, longissimus)
In pairs, discuss and present the various formations of degrees of adjectives and how they are declined
In groups, use adjectives to compare various objects
In pairs, search and present Latin names of the Roman cultural events: festivals, theatrical performances, games, home-based ceremonies
Describe the Roman cultural events using adjectives using the apposition technique
In pairs, relate the Roman cultural events to the modern cultural events
In groups, debate on the democratic practices of ancient Rome and contemporary societies
From a Latin text, identify and convert adjectives to adverbs using suffixes: -e, -iter, -er
In groups, categorize the formed adverbs basing on their functions (i.e., manner, time, place) and create sentences that illustrate their use
Using a chosen text, work in groups to identify phrases that reflect good manners exhibited by Romans
In groups, present the identified manners in relation to your own culture
Watch a given video on a Roman cultural event and using adverbs, explain the actions of the characters
In groups, form simple sentences, then add adverbs to modify the actions of the subjects
Orally and in writing, compose short stories incorporating adverbs to describe the actions involved

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learner as he/she accurately derives nouns from verbs in the chosen Latin text
Hold a conversation with the learner to find out if he/she correctly uses verbal nouns from the chosen text in their written sentences
Evaluate the sentences looking out for: Coherence, syntax, vocabulary
Observe the learner as he/she accurately uses nouns to describe other nouns
Hold a conversation with the learner observing if he/she correctly uses nouns by apposition, predication and cases to describe other nouns
Evaluate the description looking out for: coherence, syntax, vocabulary
Observe the learner as he/she aligns the adjectives with the nouns they describe
Review the learner's description of objects looking out for: syntax, vocabulary, coherence, cooperation
Observe the learner as he/she identifies the different degrees of the adjectives with the nouns they compare
Evaluate the learner's comparison of objects looking out for: syntax, vocabulary, coherence, comparison
Observe the pairs as they list the Roman cultural events and how they relate them to the modern cultural events

Evaluate the descriptions of Roman cultural events and the debate on democratic practices looking out for: use of adjectives, accuracy, syntax, vocabulary, coherency, collaboration, attentive listening
Observe the learner as he/she converts the adjectives to adverbs
Evaluate the learner's list of adverbs converted from adjectives looking out for correctness in formation and ability to categorize them by function
Evaluate the learner's presentations on good manners in Ancient Rome and their own cultures
Observe the learner as he/she explains actions of the characters in the video
Evaluate the learner's oral/written narrative looking out for: appropriate use of adverbs, syntax, vocabulary, message, coherence, collaboration

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 1.1 Latin Nouns (4 periods); 1.2 Latin Adjectives (4 periods); 1.3 Forming Adverbs (4 periods); 1.4 Using Adverbs to Compare Actions (8 periods)

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 2: PARTS OF SPEECH (CONJUNCTIONS AND VERBS IN CLAUSES)

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates effective understanding of the clauses in Latin sentences and develops reading skills to understand Latin texts and recalls the content.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a. construct complex sentences from simple clauses
b. use compound sentences to describe agriculture in the ancient Roman society

suggested_learning_activities.description: Combine suggested simple sentences into complex sentences having subordinating conjunctions of time (cum, dum, postquam, antequam/priusquam) cause (quia, quod quoniam, enim), condition (si, nisi, dummodo), contrast (quamquam, etsi, tamen), purpose (ut, ne), comparison (quam, ut) and other (sed, autem,)
Modify given sentences using subordinate conjunctions while maintaining original meaning
Ascertain the various agricultural practices in the Roman society
In pairs discuss how Romans practised agriculture, and then present your findings to the class in Latin
Write a short essay relating the Roman agricultural practices with the contemporary agricultural practices using compound sentences

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learner as he/she combines suggested simple sentences into compound sentences
Hold a conversation with the learner observing if he/she correctly uses conjunctions to combine sentences
Evaluate the learner's sentences looking out for: syntax, conjunction, vocabulary, message, coherence, collaboration
Observe the learner as he/she ascertains the various agricultural practices in the Roman society
Evaluate the learner's essay looking out for: syntax, vocabulary, message, coherence, conjunctions, critical thinking

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 3: SYNTAX IN WRITING SKILLS (Part 1 — Term 1)

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates the skill of using nouns, pronouns and verbs to construct sentences following the Latin sentence structure.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a. identify the functions of nouns, verbs, pronouns, and adjectives in a Latin sentence
b. orally and in writing, express opinions on social aspects of life; education, health, road and water transport
c. read and translate a text about social services in a Roman setting (demonstrating comprehension and contextual understanding)
a. demonstrate comprehension and accurate usage of partitive genitives in a Latin passage
b. demonstrate comprehension and accurate application of prolative verbs (ire, vadere, exire, mittere, ferre, etc.) in social life situations

suggested_learning_activities.description: From authentic Latin texts (e.g. Cicero, Caesar, etc.) analyse the functions of all nouns, verbs pronouns and adjectives within their syntactical contexts
Complete sentences by filling in grammatically correct parts of speech that are contextually appropriate
Using various sentences, describe a picture of a Roman scene
From a chosen text, identify the nouns, verbs and adjectives relating to a specific social aspect of life
In groups, discuss and present on at least one of the following social aspects of life: education, health, road transport, water transport, church
Read a Latin text about social services in Roman society and translate it into English
From a chosen Latin text, identify and categorize the genitives based on their usage (i.e., partitive, possessive, descriptive)
In groups, paraphrase sentences with partitive genitives into their equivalents
In groups, discuss and present a description of an event in social life using partitive genitives
From a given Latin text about travel and transport, identify prolative verbs (simple and compound)
In pairs, translate a text about travel, transport and communication from English to Latin
In groups, debate on a given motion about travel, transport and communication in Uganda

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learner as he/she analyses sentences from authentic Latin texts
Hold a conversation with the learner observing if he/she completes sentences with correct parts of speech
Evaluate the learner's description of pictures looking out for: syntax, accuracy, vocabulary, message, independent learning
Observe the learner as he/she identifies nouns, verbs and adjectives that relate to social aspects of life
Evaluate the learner's presentations looking out for: syntax, coherence, vocabulary, message, collaboration, communication
Observe the learner as he/she translates a text related to social aspects of life
Evaluate the learner's translation looking out for: syntax, accuracy, vocabulary, message, communication
Observe the learner as he/she identifies and categorises genitives
Evaluate the learner's presentation looking out for: syntax, accuracy, coherence, vocabulary, message, collaboration, communication
Observe the learner as he/she identifies and categorises prolative verbs
Evaluate the learner's debate looking out for: syntax, coherence, vocabulary, message, collaboration, communication

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics covered in Term 1: 3.1 Syntax (6 periods); 3.2 Partitive Genitives and Prolative Verbs (8 periods). Topic continues in Term 2.

themes.theme_title: Latin Language — Advanced Syntax and Introduction to Prose
themes.theme_description: Continuation of syntax in writing skills, covering interrogatives, commands, clause types, and translation. Introduction to Latin prose including biography, comprehension, figurative styles and mood.

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 3: SYNTAX IN WRITING SKILLS (Continued from Term 1)

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates the skill of using nouns, pronouns and verbs to construct sentences following the Latin sentence structure.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a. familiarise him/herself with different ways of asking question (-ne, Nonne, Num) including the use of interrogative pronouns, adjectives and adverbs
a. comprehend and produce direct (imperative mood) and indirect commands using prolative verbs
b. comprehend and formulate negative imperatives to prohibit (including the use of noli and nolite)

a. exhibit comprehension and appropriate usage of temporal clauses with appropriate conjunctions (cum, dum, ubi, postquam, antequam, priusquam, simul ac/simul atque, quotiens, ut donec, cum primum, quando) in the indicative mood, present tense
b. exhibit comprehension and appropriate usage of concessive clauses with appropriate conjunctions (quamquam, etiamsi, quamvis, cum, ut, licet) in the indicative mood, present tense
c. exhibit comprehension and appropriate usage of comparative clauses with appropriate conjunctions (quam, ut, quasi, velut, tamquam, sicut) in the indicative mood, present tense
a. translate texts on environment (climate change and sustainable living)
a. orally and in writing, expresses feelings of fear using appropriate verbs, adjectives and adverbs

suggested_learning_activities.description: Ascertain the three ways of asking questions to get a yes or a no answer and the use of interrogative pronouns, adjectives and adverbs
Formulate suitable questions to respective responses in a job interview dialogue
In pairs, ask and answer questions about personal life
Identify direct and indirect commands from a written/recorded conversation
Role plays a dialogue where a superior commands and the subject responds appropriately
Formulate, orally/in writing, several positive polite commands that are used in a home setting
Use the internet to find out prohibitive Latin proverbs/sayings
Uses the various ways of prohibitions to change provided positive commands to negative form
In groups, identify prohibition signs in public places and present their interpretation to the class
In groups, from a chosen text, identify conjunctions, adverbs and phrases of time
Fill in the appropriate conjunction and/or verb forms to complete temporal clauses
In groups, discuss and present school daily routines, incorporating temporal clauses in the indicative present tense
Use the internet to identify conjunctions that are used in the concessive clauses
Translate a passage where concessive clauses are used
Construct sentences with the identified conjunctions
In groups, engage in a debate on a given motion using concessive clauses
From the internet, identify conjunctions used to construct comparative clauses
Translate comparative clauses from Latin to English and vice versa
Compare real or imaginary situations using comparative clauses
Identify vocabulary particular to environment from a short-adapted texts
In groups, translate Latin texts on environmental issues
Compose a short text on a given aspect on environment
Engage in a class discussion brainstorming the various vocabularies used to express fear
Watch a video and name the various expressions of fear exhibited by the actors
Prepare and present a short story about a situation where he/she experienced fear

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learner as he/she ascertains the three ways of asking questions
Evaluate the learner's conversation looking out for: syntax, pronunciation, audibility, accuracy, coherence, vocabulary, message, collaboration, communication
Observe the learner as he/she identifies direct and indirect commands
Evaluate the learner's command formulations looking out for: syntax, pronunciation, audibility, coherence, vocabulary, message, communication
Evaluate the learner's presentation looking out for: syntax, pronunciation, audibility, coherence, vocabulary, message, communication
Observe the learner as he/she identifies temporal indicators in the text
Evaluate the learners' presentations looking out for: syntax, pronunciation, audibility, coherence, vocabulary, message, communication, collaboration
Observe the learner as he/she identifies conjunctions
Evaluate the learners' debate looking out for: syntax, pronunciation, concession, audibility, coherence, vocabulary, message, communication, collaboration
Observe the learner as he/she identifies vocabulary about environment
Evaluate the learner's composition looking out for: syntax, coherence, vocabulary, message, collaboration, cohesion
Observe the learner as he/she he discovers expressions of fear
Evaluate the learner's story, looking out for: accuracy, vocabulary, syntax, coherence, pronunciation, message

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 3.3 Asking Questions (6 periods); 3.4 Commands and Prohibitions (8 periods); 3.5 Clauses with Indicatives (8 periods); 3.6 Translating Information on Environment (6 periods); 3.7 Expressions of Fear (6 periods)

topics.core_competency: The learner develops a critical and analytical mind to make an informed judgment on issues pertaining to real life.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a. identify and describe key elements (structure, style, and purpose) of a Latin prose
b. identify author's biography and its significance to their prose work
a. identify the various themes present in a given Latin prose passage
b. identify the setting and context that influence prose
c. demonstrate comprehension and accurate usage of vocabulary and expressions used in a prose passage
d. recognise the author's target audience from the prose text
e. infer moral lessons for self and others from a prose text
a. demonstrate knowledge of various figurative styles (metaphor, personification, symbolism, hyperbole, rhetorical questions, proverbs, irony, and idioms) and their significance in Latin prose
b. relate with Roman cultural references in prose (Roman names, religion, philosophy, politics, family, games, school, customs, festivals, etc.)
a. identify the different kind of mood portrayed in the passage and discuss its significance
b. appreciate the impression prose creates on a reader

suggested_learning_activities.description: Break down a given prose passage into its key structural components (e.g., introduction, development, climax, resolution)
Describe the various features by which the structural elements of a prose passage can be identified
From the internet, identify key components of the biography of a given prose's author
In a group, create a timeline of the author's life, highlighting key events, historical context, and major works
In Latin, compose a short essay on the author's life and how it influenced features and components of the prose

From a given prose passage, identify any available themes (Moral/ethical values, Politics, leadership, war, heroism, religion/divinity, philosophy, love, parenting, grief/loss, nature/universe, education, history, law, mortality, legacy, discipline)
Match the various expressions and vocabulary in the text to the identified themes
With justification, rank themes in order of importance based on their prominence in the text
Identify the time-and-place setting, cultural, historical and social background of the prose text
Give a speech on how the identified setting contributes to the mood and tone of the prose passage
Compare the nature of a prose passage to its equivalents in contemporary society
In groups, explain the meaning and significance of words, expressions and idioms used in a given text
Compose a short text using vocabulary and expressions borrowed from the given prose passage
Read the text and identify the target audience of the prose passage based on its language, style and themes
Rewrite a section of the prose to suit a different audience, while preserving its core message
Identify the lessons that can be drawn from the prose passage
In the first and third persons, construct short sentences that convey the moral lessons drawn from the prose passage
Write a friendly letter describing your experience with the prose passage highlighting the key features, author, and moral lessons
Identify the various figurative styles commonly used by authors of prose
In groups, discuss the application of figurative styles in a given prose passage
Discuss how figurative language enhances the meaning, tone, and atmosphere of a prose passage
From the prose, identify Roman cultural elements that can be of interest to a contemporary person
Write a letter as if he/she were a Roman citizen from the era responding to events or practices described in prose
Identify stylistic devices: literary devices, verb moods (imperative, subjunctive), specific verbs used to communication emotions
Analyse the different emotions (anger, happy, sad, moody, flat, excited, anxious) exhibited by the characters in the prose
Compose a short poem capturing the mood of one of the characters in a prose piece

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learner as he/she identifies key components of the authors biography
Evaluate the learner's composition evaluating: accuracy, vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message
Observe the learner as he/she identifies themes in a prose passage
Evaluate the learner's matching and ranking activities looking out for: vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message, accuracy
Observe the learner as he/she identifies the setting and context of the prose passage
Evaluate the learner's comparison looking out for: vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message
Evaluate the learner's composition looking out for: accuracy, vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message, communication, collaboration
Evaluate the learner's letter writing looking out for: accuracy, vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message, communication
Observe the learner as he/she identifies the figurative styles used by authors
Evaluate the learner's modification looking out for: accuracy, vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message
Evaluate the learner's letter writing looking out for: accuracy, vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message, communication
Observe the learner as he/she identifies the common literary devices
Evaluate the learner's discussion looking out for: accuracy, vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message, communication, collaboration
Evaluate the learner's prose composition looking out for: accuracy, vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message, communication

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 4.1 Biography of An Author of Prose (4 periods); 4.2 Comprehension of Prose (8 periods); 4.3 Figurative Styles in Prose (6 periods); 4.4 The Mood in Prose (4 periods)

themes.theme_description: Introduction to Roman plays, examining historical background, characteristics of Roman theatre in the Golden Age, and the evolution of drama into the medieval period.

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates creative thinking to appreciate the value of drama for their aesthetic and imaginative growth and development of a critical and analytical mind to make an informed judgment.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: describe a historical background to Roman drama, including key developments and influences
a. identify the characteristics and significance of Roman theatre
b. appreciate the different forms and unique features of Roman theatre
a. explain how Roman drama evolved during the medieval period, highlighting key developments
b. demonstrate knowledge of various types, characteristics and significance of Roman drama during the medieval period
c. demonstrate knowledge of characteristics of medieval drama and its significance in the cultural context

suggested_learning_activities.description: On YouTube (TED-Ed, History Time, Crash Course, Khan Academy, etc.), watch a video such as e.g. Ancient Roman theatre, Roman Drama: Comedy, Tragedy, and the Stage, Roman theatre Explained: Plautus, Terence, and Seneca
From the video, identify origin and development of Roman drama, features of theatre and costumes, social and political significances, genres and various playwrights
In groups, compose a set of short questions and answers highlighting major features and notable authors of Roman drama
Identify images and names of various Roman theatres and the key Roman festivals associated with them
From chosen pictures of Roman theatre, in short Latin sentences, describe features (e.g. scaenae frons, orchestra, and cavea) and the significance of each
In groups, create short presentations on a specific characteristic (architecture, music and dance, etc.) of Roman theatre and how they impacted on performance
Write short paragraphs about the influence of Greek drama, Etruscan traditions and Roman religious festivals on Roman theatre
From a chosen documentary, identify various forms (Tragoedia, comoedia, togata, Atellan Farce, Mime et Pantomime) of Roman theatre
Present a slide presentation showing how features of Roman theatre can benefit the Music Industry in Uganda
Identify development of drama in the medieval era from a provided text
In groups, create a timeline illustrating major shifts in drama during the medieval period
In groups, discuss how factors that led to the persistence of Roman theatre in the medieval times apply to the creative arts industry in Uganda
From a text, identify descriptions of various types of medieval drama, including liturgical drama, morality plays, and secular farces
In groups, perform short skits highlighting key characteristics of medieval drama
Categorise plays based on their themes, settings, and audiences, using the examples provided
From key excerpts, identify key features (such as religious themes, allegorical figures, and community involvement) of medieval plays

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learner as he/she watches a video that describes roman plays
Hold a conversation with the learner observing if he/she successfully identifies origin, features, and development of Roman drama
Evaluate the learner as he/she engages in question and answers looking out for: accuracy, vocabulary, coherence, message, communication, collaboration
Observe the learner during group discussions and hold a conversation with him/her to guide discussions on the significance of architectural features, influences and festivals
Test the learner's ability to identify and to explain the characteristics and significance of Roman theatre
Evaluate the learner's written paragraph on the major influences of Roman theatre
Observe the learner as he/she identifies the developments of drama in the medieval era
Evaluate the learner's discussion looking out for: accuracy, vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message, communication, collaboration
Evaluate the learner's performance looking out for: accuracy, vocabulary, syntax, coherence, message, communication, collaboration
